# Known vulnerabilities

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/vulnerability_report.py. Do not edit by hand:
     the next scan overwrites it. Change the script instead. -->

> [!CAUTION]
> These images are vulnerable on purpose. They are museum pieces, not something to
> patch. This page counts how bad it is, so that nobody has to guess. It changes
> nothing about the rule in the README: loopback only, no real data, never exposed.

On the 1st and 15th of each month a workflow builds an SBOM (software bill of
materials) for every image a stack runs and checks it for known vulnerabilities.
[Syft](https://github.com/anchore/syft) lists what is installed.
[Grype](https://github.com/anchore/grype) looks each item up in the Debian, Alpine,
GitHub and NVD advisory data.

Each number is the count of **distinct** vulnerabilities in an image. A CVE that
hits several packages, or is reported by several sources, is counted once, at its
worst severity.

Numbers go up even when an image does not change, because new CVEs are published
against old software every week. The *Change* column says which of the two it
was: *same image* means the advisory data grew, *image rebuilt* means the image did.

## Declared components

Syft finds software through package records and version strings in binaries.
Anything compiled from source or unpacked from an archive can leave neither, and
then no scanner sees it. So the SBOM of each image also lists, by hand, the
components this project knows are in it. They are kept in
[`images.json`](../.github/vulnerability-scan/images.json), each with the reason it is
there and, where this project vendors it, the checksum of its source archive.

A declared component is only added when Syft did not find the same product and
version itself. In the tables, `declared` marks the vulnerabilities that only
these entries reveal.

| Image | Added to the SBOM in this scan |

| `typo3:3.3.0` | `pcre 7.7`, `typo3/cms 3.3.0` |
| `typo3:3.8.1` | `typo3/cms 3.8.1` |

| `mysql:5.5` | none needed |

## How far to trust these numbers

Some vulnerabilities are still not counted:

- Older TYPO3 releases are thinly covered. NVD has CPE data for some old TYPO3 CVEs and GitHub's advisories rarely reach before 6.2. The full record is TYPO3's own [security bulletins](https://typo3.org/help/security-advisories), which have no machine-readable feed.
- The third-party code every TYPO3 release bundles in `typo3/contrib/`, such as JavaScript libraries and mailers, is not declared yet. The exceptions are the two Composer libraries 6.2.31 pins.
- PHP 4.4.9's bundled GD and its bundled MySQL client 3.23.49 are not declared. NVD files GD issues in PHP's copy under PHP itself, and a CPE for the 3.23 client would match MySQL server CVEs that do not apply to it.

Others are counted that may not apply. Matching by CPE asks NVD which versions a
CVE affects, and nothing more. So a PHP CVE in an extension these images never
compiled, or a MySQL CVE in a feature the stacks never use, is still counted.
That mostly affects the `declared` and `binary` rows.

So the numbers are an estimate. They are not a precise total and not a guaranteed
floor. The trend across scans is more reliable than any single number.

## How this page is made

[`.github/workflows/vulnerability-scan.yml`](../.github/workflows/vulnerability-scan.yml)
runs Syft on each published image in GHCR, adds the declared components, scans the
complete SBOM with Grype, and writes one summary per scan to
[`vulnerability-scans/`](vulnerability-scans/). This page is rendered from all of
them.

The complete SBOMs, in CycloneDX format, and Grype's full reports are kept as
workflow artifacts for 90 days, for anyone who wants the CVE list behind a number.
To scan right now, run the workflow by hand.

## The SBOMs in the registry

Each SBOM is also attached to its image in GHCR as a signed attestation. Only an image that is new, or whose SBOM changed, gets a new
one. Check that an image's SBOM came from this workflow:

```sh
gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/mteu/typo3-throwback/typo3:3.3.0 \
  --repo mteu/typo3-throwback \
  --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom
```

Add `--format json` to get the SBOM itself. A private fork skips this step:
GitHub offers attestations in private repositories only to organizations on
GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
